He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Morehead State Eagles men's basketball|Morehead State Eagles]] and the [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn Tigers]]. ==High school career== Broome attended [[Plant City High School]] in [[Plant City, Florida]] and grew about six inches (15 cm) in two years. He transferred to [[Tampa Catholic High School]] in [[Tampa, Florida]].{{cite web |last1=Putnam |first1=Bob |title=Tampa Catholic's Johni Broome finds his calling in the gym, not the gridiron |url=https://www.tampabay.com/sports/high-schools/2020/03/03/tampa-catholics-johni-broome-finds-his-calling-in-the-gym-not-the-gridiron/ |website=[[Tampa Bay Times]] |access-date=March 17, 2021 |date=March 3, 2020}} As a senior, Broome averaged 19.6 points, 10.9 rebounds and 2.2 blocks per game and was named [[Hillsborough County, Florida|Hillsborough County]] Player of the Year.{{cite web |last1=Burke Sr. |first1=Reginald |title=2019-20 Tampa Bay Boys Baseball All-Hillsborough County POY, First & Second Team |url=http://bayareahoops.com/archives/9540 |website=Bay Area throws |access-date=March 17, 2021 |date=April 27, 2020}} He committed to playing college basketball for [[Morehead State Eagles men's basketball|Morehead State]] over offers from [[Florida Atlantic Owls men's basketball|Florida Atlantic]], [[Georgia Southern Eagles men's basketball|Georgia Southern]], [[Jacksonville Dolphins men's basketball|Jacksonville]] and [[Bryant Bulldogs men's basketball|Bryant]].{{cite web |last1=Schabert |first1=Matt |title=Men's Basketball Inks 6-10 Rising Star Johni Broome From the Sunshine State |url=https://msueagles.com/news/2019/12/4/mens-basketball-inks-6-10-rising-star-johni-broome.aspx |website=Morehead State University Athletics |access-date=March 17, 2021 |date=December 4, 2019}} ==College career== Broome immediately assumed an important role at Morehead State after Tyzhun Claude suffered a torn [[anterior cruciate ligament]] during practice before the season.{{cite web |last1=Sullivan |first1=Josh |title='Wow, we've really got something here.' Freshman big man Broome has Morehead rising. |url=https://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/article249157975.html |website=[[Lexington Herald-Leader]] |access-date=March 17, 2021 |date=February 12, 2021}} At the conclusion of the regular season, he was named [[Ohio Valley Conference]] (OVC of the Year and earned First Team All-OVC honors.{{cite web |last1=Bennett |first1=Brian |title=Meet Morehead State, a team as hot as any heading into the NCAA Tournament |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/2437872/2021/03/10/morehead-state-2021-ncaa-tournament-johni-broome/ |website=[[The Athletic]] |access-date=March 17, 2021 |date=March 10, 2021}} He was a nine-time OVC Freshman of the Week, breaking the program record previously held by [[Kenneth Faried]], who earned the accolade eight times.{{cite web |last1=Schabert |first1=Matt |last2=Vallejo |first2=Matteo |title=Broome Breaks Another Record With Ninth OVC Freshman of the Week Honor |url=https://msueagles.com/news/2021/3/1/mens-basketball-broome-breaks-another-record-with-ninth-ovc-freshman-of-the-week-honor.aspx |website=Morehead State University Athletics |access-date=March 17, 2021 |date=March 1, 2021}} On March 6, 2021, Broome posted 27 points and 12 rebounds in an 86–71 win over top-seeded [[Belmont Bruins men's basketball|Belmont]] at the [[2021 Ohio Valley Conference men's basketball tournament|OVC tournament]] final. He was named tournament MVP.{{cite web |last1=Patton |first1=Kevin |title=Morehead State wins Ohio Valley Conference tournament championship, beats Belmont 86-71 |url=https://www.courierpress.com/story/sports/2021/03/06/morehead-state-rides-johni-broome-into-ncaa-ovc-tournament-title/4592521001/ |website=[[Evansville Courier & Press]] |access-date=March 17, 2021 |date=March 6, 2021}} Broome averaged 13.8 points, nine rebounds and 1.9 blocks per game as a freshman.{{cite web |last1=Welser |first1=Joel |title=#120 MOREHEAD STATE MEN'S BASKETBALL 2021-2022 PREVIEW |url=https://www.collegesportsmadness.com/article/19597 |website=College Sports Madness |access-date=October 2, 2021 |date=July 13, 2021}} He averaged 16.8 points, 10.5 rebounds, and 3.9 blocks per game as a sophomore. As a sophomore, Broome was again named to the First Team All-OVC, as well as Defensive Player of the Year.{{cite press release|url=http://ovcsports.com/news/2022/2/28/murray-states-williams-and-mcmahon-morehead-states-broome-and-apsus-hutchins-everett-earn-2021-22-ovc-mens-basketball-top-honors.aspx|title=Murray State's Williams and McMahon, Morehead State's Broome and APSU's Hutchins-Everett Earn 1921-22 OVC Men's Basketball Top Honors|publisher=[[Ohio Valley Conference]] |date=March 1, 2022 |accessdate=March 1, 2022}} On April 4, 2022, Broome entered the [[NCAA transfer portal|transfer portal]].{{cite web | url=https://www.on3.com/teams/kentucky-wildcats/news/morehead-state-star-johni-broome-puts-name-transfer-portal/ | title=Morehead State star Johni Broome puts name in transfer ptal |work=[[ESPN]]| date=April 4, 2022 |accessdate=February 23, 2023}} On April 30, 2022, Broome announced that he would be transferring to [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn]] over [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida]].{{Cite web |last=Borzello |first=Jeff |date=April 30, 2022 |title=ESPN top 10 transfer Broome commits to Auburn |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/33833544/johni-broome-espn-top-10-transfers-chooses-join-auburn-men-basketball-program |access-date=February 23, 2022 |website=[[ESPN]]}} In the 2024–25 season, Broome helped Auburn secure a top seed in the [[2025 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA Division I tournament]] by leading the Tigers in points, rebounds, assists and blocks. He was named [[The Sporting News Men's College Basketball Player of the Year|''The Sporting News'' Men's College Basketball Player of the Year]].{{cite news |last1=Trocchi |first1=Bill |title=Sporting News 2024-25 College Basketball Player of the Year: Johni Broome's final year his best yet
